prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Do you mean (A) a plain‑English site that teaches crypto basics and uses real, verifiable numbers in its lessons (charts, on‑chain metrics, historical examples), or (B) an educator/newsletter that publicly posts its own tracked trades/portfolio and shows both gains and losses? Those are different things — I can point you to the best options for either.

Quick recommendations:

If you want plain‑English beginner education (clear explanations, good for learning fundamentals)
- Coinbase Learn — very simple, non‑technical primers and short explainers.
- Kraken Learn / Binance Academy — approachable, vendor‑backed tutorials and glossaries.
- Investopedia’s crypto section — plain language with cross‑links to other finance topics.
- Coin Bureau — long, readable guides and videos aimed at beginners.

If you want data‑driven resources that show real numbers (charts, on‑chain metrics, market P&L)
- Glassnode and Coin Metrics — on‑chain data providers with clear charts and historical metrics.
- Messari and IntoTheBlock — research + quant metrics with downloadable data and explanations.
- Nansen — wallet‑level analytics (good for following what large holders or smart money do).

If you specifically want educators who publish their own track records or “show their losses”
- Look for independent newsletters/Substacks or bloggers that (a) publish an audited track record, (b) post links to public wallet addresses or exchange proof, or (c) provide verifiable backtests. Many good teachers don’t publish personal P&L for legal/ethical reasons, so you’ll mostly find this among a few independent writers or traders — search Substack and check their transparency page before trusting them.

How to verify “publishes losses” / transparency
- Public wallet addresses or exchange statements you can verify.
- Audited track records (third‑party attestation).
- Clear methodology, timeframes, and admission of losing trades / drawdowns.
- No pay‑to‑see “perfect” results (avoid services that only show cherry‑picked winners).

If you tell me whether you want general learning materials vs. a people/ newsletter that shows an audited P&L, I’ll give a short, specific list you can trust.
